name: Senso-ji Temple, Asakusa
why: Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 628) through the giant red Kaminarimon lantern. Busy by day, quietly magical lit up at night when the crowds go home.
tips: Go after 7 pm: the buildings are lit and the shopping street is shut
Nakamise snacks: ningyo-yaki and age-manju

name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
why: A forest shrine in the middle of the city: 100,000 trees donated from all over Japan, a gravel path under a huge wooden torii, sake barrels stacked as offerings.
tips: Opens around sunrise and closes at sunset
Pair with Harajuku and Omotesando in one walk

name: Shibuya Crossing & Shibuya Sky
localName: 渋谷スクランブル交差点
why: The famous scramble: up to 3,000 people crossing at once. Watch from above at Shibuya Sky's open rooftop, 230 m up, best at sunset.
tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out: book a few days ahead online (about ¥2,500)
The crossing itself is free and best at 6–8 pm
mapsQuery: Shibuya Crossing & Shibuya Sky, Tokyo, Japan

name: Golden Gai, Shinjuku
why: Six narrow alleys, 200-odd bars, some with five seats. Postwar Tokyo frozen in place. Bourdain's kind of neighborhood.
tips: Many bars charge a seating fee (¥500–1,500)
Look for 'Welcome' or English signs; some are regulars-only

name: Omoide Yokocho, Shinjuku
why: 'Memory Lane': a smoky alley of yakitori counters beside the Shinjuku tracks. Elbow room is optional.
tips: Cash
Order a beer and a few skewers, then move to the next stall

name: teamLab Planets, Toyosu
localName: チームラボプラネッツ
why: Barefoot through rooms of light, water and mirrors. Gimmicky on paper, genuinely beautiful in person.
tips: Timed tickets sell out on weekends: book about a week ahead
You'll wade knee-deep: wear shorts or roll-up pants

name: Tokyo National Museum, Ueno
why: Japan's biggest collection of samurai armor, swords, screens and Buddhist sculpture. If you only do one museum, make it this.
tips: Closed Mondays
The Honkan (main building) has the greatest hits in two floors
mapsQuery: Tokyo National Museum, Ueno, Tokyo, Japan

name: Ueno Park & Ameyoko
why: Temples, a five-story pagoda and museums in one park, with Ameyoko next door: a rowdy postwar market street of fish, snacks and standing bars.
tips: Ameyoko is best late afternoon
Cheap seafood rice bowls along the tracks

name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
why: The old Edo Castle grounds: massive stone walls, moats and a free garden where the shogun's keep once stood.
tips: Free
Closed Mondays and Fridays
mapsQuery: Imperial Palace East Gardens, Tokyo, Japan

name: Yanaka Old Town
why: One of the few neighborhoods that survived the war and the 1923 quake: temples, cats, a shotengai of old shops and a huge, peaceful cemetery.
tips: Start at Nippori station, walk to Yanaka Ginza at sunset
Menchi-katsu (fried meat cutlet) from the street

name: Ryogoku Kokugikan & sumo
why: The sumo hall. No tournament in late October (the November tournament is in Fukuoka, around Nov 8–22), but the free sumo museum and chanko restaurants make Ryogoku worth an hour.
tips: Morning sumo practice at some stables can be watched with a tour

name: Akihabara
why: Electronics, anime, retro games and maid cafes. Even if it's not your thing, Super Potato's retro-game floors are a trip.
tips: Sunday afternoons the main street goes car-free
Retro game shops: Super Potato, Beep

name: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka
localName: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
why: Miyazaki's own whimsical museum, with a short film you can only see here. Tickets go on sale the 10th of the month before.
tips: November tickets went on sale Oct 10: check Lawson Ticket for leftovers
Closed Tuesdays

name: Tokyo Tower & Zojo-ji
why: The orange 1958 tower rising behind a 600-year-old temple of the Tokugawa shoguns. The best photo in Tokyo is from Zojo-ji's gate at dusk.
tips: Zojo-ji is free; the tower deck is about ¥1,200

name: Kappabashi Kitchen Street
why: Where Tokyo's chefs shop: knives, lacquerware, and the plastic food models you see in restaurant windows. A knife here beats any souvenir.
tips: Kamata and Kama-Asa for knives; they'll engrave your name
Most shops close Sundays

name: Nezu Shrine
why: A tunnel of small red torii gates and a 1706 lacquered shrine, without Kyoto's crowds.
tips: Free
10 minutes' walk from Yanaka

name: Shimokitazawa
why: Tokyo's thrift-shop, live-music, tiny-bar neighborhood. Good for an aimless afternoon and a cheap gig at night.
tips: Live houses: Shelter, Club Que, 251
Vintage shops open around noon

name: Hama-rikyu Gardens
why: A shogun's duck-hunting garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond, skyscrapers behind it. Matcha and a sweet at Nakajima-no-ochaya.
tips: Water bus to Asakusa leaves from inside the garden

name: Fuunji (tsukemen), Shinjuku
why: Thick dipping noodles in a rich chicken-and-fish broth. There's always a line of office workers, and it moves fast.
tips: Buy a ticket at the machine first
Ask for the soup-wari (broth top-up) at the end

name: Afuri, Ebisu
why: Light yuzu-shio ramen: citrusy, clean, perfect when you've had enough rich food. Open late.
tips: Vegan option available

name: Tonki, Meguro
why: A 1939 tonkatsu counter where a team of white-capped cooks works in silence. Crisp pork cutlet, refills of rice and cabbage.
tips: Closed Tuesdays
They take your order while you wait in line

name: Sushi at Toyosu Market
why: Breakfast sushi a few hundred meters from the tuna auction. Sushi Dai has the famous line; Daiwa Sushi and others next door are just as fresh.
tips: Go before 7 am or after 11 am
Closed Sundays and market holidays
mapsQuery: Sushi at Toyosu Market, Tokyo, Japan

name: Tsunahachi Tempura, Shinjuku
why: Since 1924: tempura fried in front of you at the counter, one piece at a time. Lunch sets are a bargain.
tips: Sit at the counter
Lunch set around ¥1,800

name: Uogashi Nihon-ichi standing sushi
why: Standing sushi bar: order piece by piece from the chef, eat, leave. Fresh, cheap and very Tokyo.
tips: Many branches; Shibuya and Shinjuku are handy
Point at the menu boards
mapsQuery: Uogashi Nihon-ichi standing sushi, Tokyo, Japan

name: Yakitori Ton Ton, Yurakucho
why: Smoky yakitori and beer under the train tracks at Yurakucho, with salarymen at plastic tables. Pure Tokyo after dark.
tips: Cash; many stalls under the tracks

name: Ichiran Ramen
why: Tonkotsu ramen in private booths, ordered on a form. Open 24 hours. Fun once, but locals call it the tourist ramen.
tips: Always open
Fill in the form: firmness, richness, spice

name: Naniwaya Sohonten taiyaki, Azabu-Juban
why: Fish-shaped cakes with sweet red bean, made one at a time in iron molds since 1909. The original taiyaki shop.
tips: Closed Tuesdays
Near Sarashina Horii soba
mapsQuery: Naniwaya Sohonten taiyaki, Azabu-Juban, Tokyo, Japan

name: Mihashi anmitsu, Ueno
why: Classic anmitsu: agar jelly, sweet beans, fruit and black sugar syrup. Old-Tokyo dessert in a no-frills shop.
tips: Opposite Ueno Park's south entrance

name: Suzukien matcha gelato, Asakusa
why: Matcha gelato in seven strengths. No. 7 is said to be the world's most intense matcha ice cream.
tips: Try No. 7 and a lighter one side by side
mapsQuery: Suzukien matcha gelato, Asakusa, Tokyo, Japan

name: Isetan Shinjuku depachika sweets
localName: 伊勢丹新宿 デパ地下
why: The basement food hall of Isetan: pastry counters, wagashi, perfect fruit. A dessert crawl with no reservations needed.
tips: Weekday evenings are calmer
mapsQuery: Isetan Shinjuku depachika sweets, Tokyo, Japan

name: Ginza West
why: A 1947 coffee-and-cake salon: white tablecloths, leaf pies and dry cake. Postwar Ginza elegance.

name: Chatei Hatou, Shibuya
why: Dim, wood-paneled kissaten where each cup is hand-poured and served in a cup chosen to suit you. A Tokyo classic.
tips: No laptops; quiet room

name: Glitch Coffee, Jimbocho
why: Some of the best light-roast pour-over in Tokyo, in the city's old bookstore district.
tips: Pair with a browse of Jimbocho's used bookshops

name: Cafe de l’Ambre, Ginza
localName: カフェ・ド・ランブル
why: Coffee only, since 1948. The founder aged beans for decades. Order the Blanc et Noir, an iced coffee with milk in a champagne coupe.
tips: Coffee only, no food
Cash
mapsQuery: Cafe de l’Ambre, Ginza, Tokyo, Japan

name: Fuglen Tokyo, Tomigaya
why: Norwegian cafe by day, cocktail bar by night, in a quiet corner near Yoyogi Park.

name: Kayaba Coffee, Yanaka
why: A 1938 wooden coffee house on a Yanaka corner, revived. Egg sandwich and a coffee on the tatami upstairs.

name: Ebisu Yokocho
why: A covered alley of tiny bars and food stalls, loud and friendly. Easy to talk to strangers.
tips: Gets packed after 8 pm

name: Bar BenFiddich, Shinjuku
why: A candle-lit bar where the bartender grows and grinds his own herbs and builds cocktails from scratch. One of Asia's best.
tips: Small: go early or expect to wait
No menu; tell him what you like

name: Popeye craft beer, Ryogoku
why: Seventy Japanese craft beers on tap. A beer pilgrimage spot for 30 years.
tips: Happy hour early evening
mapsQuery: Popeye craft beer, Ryogoku, Tokyo, Japan

name: Nonbei Yokocho, Shibuya
why: 'Drunkard's alley' beside the Shibuya tracks: lantern-lit bars with six seats each.
tips: Seating charges common

name: Shinbashi salaryman bars (baseball on TV)
why: Shinbashi's salaryman bars put NPB on every screen. Watch the away Series games here with the locals.
tips: Shinbashi station west exit, under the tracks

name: Toyosu Market tuna auction
why: Where Tsukiji's wholesale market moved in 2018. Watch the tuna auction from the observation deck at dawn.
tips: The lower viewing deck needs an online lottery (apply about a month ahead); the upper gallery is free
Closed Sundays and market holidays
mapsQuery: Toyosu Market tuna auction, Tokyo, Japan

name: Ameyoko Market
why: A clattering market street under the tracks: dried fish, fruit on sticks, discount sneakers, standing bars.

name: Nakameguro & Daikanyama
why: Canal-side boutiques, Tsutaya bookstore's beautiful Daikanyama shop, and good coffee everywhere.

name: Jakotsu-yu sento, Asakusa
why: A neighborhood bathhouse fed by real hot-spring water, with a little outdoor bath. Tokyo's everyday bath culture, about ¥550.
tips: Bring a small towel or buy one there
Closed Tuesdays

name: Spa LaQua, Tokyo Dome City
why: A big modern onsen complex with outdoor baths and saunas. A good reset after the flight.
mapsQuery: Spa LaQua, Tokyo Dome City, Tokyo, Japan

name: Yoyogi Park
why: Big, open and local on weekends: rockabilly dancers, drummers, picnics. Next to Meiji Jingu.

name: Rikugien Garden
why: An Edo-era stroll garden and one of Tokyo's best for autumn color. Maples light up at night in late November.
tips: Best color late Nov–early Dec

name: Kamata Onsen (black-water sento)
why: A 1937 neighborhood bathhouse with some of Ota ward's darkest 'black water' hot spring, plus an electric bath and sauna. About ¥550, very local.
tips: About 10 min walk from Keikyu Kamata
Hours vary (roughly 10:00 to midnight or 1 am): check before going

name: Kamata hanetsuki gyoza
localName: 羽根つき餃子 蒲田
why: Kamata is the home of hanetsuki ('winged') gyoza: pan-fried dumplings joined by a lacy crisp skirt. Several old Chinese restaurants near the station compete; a plate and a beer is under ¥1,500.
tips: Look around the station's east exit

name: Haneda Terminal 3 observation deck
localName: 羽田空港 第3ターミナル 展望デッキ
why: Open 24 hours: planes taking off over Tokyo Bay, sunrise over the water, Tokyo Tower and Skytree on clear days. Free, 10 min from Kamata.
tips: 5th floor
May close in bad weather
mapsQuery: Haneda Terminal 3 observation deck, Tokyo, Japan
